column1: # Key commands explained: one line per command in roadmap.json's "commands" lists (keycmd_site.py).
# Columns (tab-separated): exact command string, safety, what this exact invocation does (<= 110 characters).
# Safety: ro = read-only (may write only its own output file: a dump, capture or report)
#         load = read-only, but its job is heavy traffic or I/O (benchmarks, wide port scans, data read-back checks)
#         ch = changes state (files, config, this shell, services that stay up or come back); opening a shell counts
#         dg = dangerous: by itself stops a service, evicts pods, destroys resources or cuts access; aimed at the
#         wrong thing, it takes a service down or locks people out. Effects that only bite later (mask) are ch.
# The build fails when a key command has no line here; tests/test_keycmd.py checks lengths and safety.
